No, it does not use a database transaction. According to [[write-journal]], the rollback capability is provided by the **in-memory write journal itself**, which serves as the transaction log for the duration of one run. The page explicitly states: "This provides all-or-nothing semantics for writes without requiring a database transaction — the in-memory journal itself serves as the transaction log."

So the rollback is purely in-memory, not backed by a database transaction.
